expectations.text: The reply begins with a progress marker identifying Phase 1.
expectations.evidence: > **Phase 1 of 5 · Explore and choose a direction**

expectations.text: The reply includes a briefing with four labeled sections covering key debates, major voices, patterns, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: The reply has four labeled sections: "**Key debates**", "**Major voices**", "**Patterns**" and "**Open questions**".

expectations.text: The briefing is roughly 300 to 500 words long (it fails if under 250 or over 600 words).
expectations.evidence: By my rough count, the briefing from "## Briefing" through the end of Open questions is about 360 words, which is inside 300–500.

expectations.text: The reply presents a mind map, either as an HTML page built from the skill's mind map template or as an indented text tree.
expectations.evidence: "I saved an interactive map to **.../mind-map.html**". The tool log shows it was built from templates/mind-map.html.

expectations.text: The mind map has 4 to 6 top-level angles, each with 2 or 3 narrower angles, and every angle has a saturation value between 0 and 1 (or, for a text tree, a crowdedness label).
expectations.evidence: In the visible part of the file, each top-level branch has 3 children, and every branch and child has a saturation value between 0 and 1 (e.g. "Academic achievement", "saturation": 0.85). The file is cut off, so I couldn't confirm the total number of top-level branches. The reply's own mention of the families and fifth-day branches is consistent with 4–6.

expectations.text: No mind map label is phrased as a research question; labels are short topics.
expectations.evidence: Labels are short topics with no question marks, e.g. "Academic achievement", "Juvenile crime", "Why districts adopt it and what it costs". Questions appear only in the separate "questions" fields.

expectations.text: The reply does not tell the user which angle they should choose or which one is best.
expectations.evidence: It only describes how crowded branches are ("Academic achievement is the most crowded branch"), then asks: "which direction pulls you most"

expectations.text: Every link in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session. Every DOI (as a doi.org link or as text) either was opened itself or appears exactly in the list of DOIs found on pages Claude opened (shown under FILES or DOIS ON OPENED PAGES). A DOI seen only in search results doesn't count. Links and DOIs in the mind map count too.
expectations.evidence: Every visible mind-map URL was fetched this session: iza.org/dp/12204, edworkingpapers ai22-630, the nwea RAND page, scholarsjunction, both edweek articles, and both ideas.repec pages. No DOIs appear in the reply.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user which direction interests them and why.
expectations.evidence: "which direction pulls you most, and why does it seem worth researching?"

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions.
expectations.evidence: There is only one question, at the end: "which direction pulls you most, and why..."
